{{draft task|Consistent overhead byte stuffing}}

The Consistent Overhead Byte Stuffing (COBS) algorithm is used to demarcate a byte stream into frames. Examples can be found in its [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consistent_Overhead_Byte_Stuffing#Encoding_examples Wikipedia article].

;Task:

To encode, instances of the byte <code>0x00</code> in the unencoded stream are substituted with the number of bytes until the next instance of <code>0x00</code> (we'll call this a milestone).
If <code>0x00</code> does not appear within the next 254 bytes after a milestone the algorithm must emit an extra milestone at the 255th byte.
Of the encoded output, the first byte is the first milestone, and the final milestone will be the number of bytes until the final byte - <code>0x00</code>.

;Bonus tasks:

* &nbsp; Decode an encoded packet
** &nbsp; Report an error if the final milestone exceeds the length of the end of the packet
* &nbsp; Support encoding with a non-zero marker
